subtitle: How the Deccan Forged Wealth from Heavy Lead and Distant Seas

panels.shot: low-angle dramatic close-up of a Satavahana Moneyer holding a large dull-grey lead coin with a tiny ship in relief, glowing against a dark map of the Deccan and the sea
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer stands in a dim mint, arm outstretched, displaying a heavy lead coin marked with a small ship, while behind him loom ghostly outlines of the Deccan plateau and curling ocean waves.

dialogue.text: In the Deccan of the Satavahanas, they minted power not in gold, but in lead, potin and ship-marked coins that tied inland hills to distant seas.

i18n.hi: सातवाहन दक्कन में सोने नहीं, सीसे, पॉटिन और जहाज़ चिन्हित सिक्कों से पहाड़ों को समंदर से जोड़ा गया।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over the rugged Deccan plateau showing mine pits, river valleys and a distant coastline haze
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer stands on a rocky outcrop above the Deccan, pointing toward clusters of lead mines in the hills and faintly visible port towns along a hazy western shoreline.

dialogue.text: The Satavahana age stretched across the Deccan, between dry plateaus and two seas, rich in ores, forests and caravan paths.

i18n.hi: सातवाहन युग दक्कन में सूखे पठारों और दो समुद्रों के बीच फैला, अयस्क, जंगल और काफ़िला-राहों से भरा।

panels.shot: intimate mid-shot inside a dim mine entrance, lantern light catching raw lead ore
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer crouches beside miners in a tunnel, watching as they pry dull, bluish chunks of lead ore from the rock walls under the flicker of oil lamps.

dialogue.text: Here, lead lay thick in the earth, easier to draw than silver, cheaper than copper, abundant in the Deccan’s veins.

i18n.hi: यहीं ज़मीन में सीसा मोटी परतों में था, चाँदी से सस्ता, ताँबे से भी आसान, दक्कन की रगों में भरपूर।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a crude rural market on packed earth, traders weighing grain and cloth with metal bits and cowries
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer stands at the edge of a bustling village market, watching cloth-sellers haggle with farmers as bits of metal, cowries and grain measures change hands in a swirl of dust.

dialogue.text: Villages and towns already traded in many ways, with grain, cloth, cowries and metal slivers. Yet the empire’s reach demanded something more regular, more trusted.

i18n.hi: गाँव और कस्बे पहले से ही अनाज, कपड़ा, कौड़ी और धातु के टुकड़ों से सौदा करते थे, पर साम्राज्य की पकड़ को चाहिए था ज़्यादा पक्का, भरोसेमंद विनिमय।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder of the Moneyer in a royal workshop, viewing a table with different metals: lead ingots, copper bars, a few silver pieces
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer studies a table where lead ingots lie in neat rows beside scarcer copper bars and a few glinting silver pieces, while artisans in the background hammer dies and test moulds.

dialogue.text: Royal workshops weighed their choices. Gold and silver were rare and hoarded. Copper was useful, but costlier. Lead, heavy and common, offered a different path.

i18n.hi: राज-कारखानों ने तोलकर सोचा—सोना-चाँदी कम और जमा हुआ, ताँबा काम का पर महँगा, भारी और आम सीसे ने नया रास्ता दिखाया।

panels.shot: close-up of molten lead being poured into shallow coin moulds, glowing against dark surroundings
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer, face lit by furnace glow, carefully guides a ladle as molten lead streams into shallow circular moulds laid out on a stone slab.

dialogue.text: So they did something few great dynasties dared: they made lead itself a main currency, casting thick, dull-grey coins for everyday exchange.

i18n.hi: फिर उन्होंने वह किया जो बड़ी रियासतें कम ही करती हैं—सीसे को ही चलन बना दिया, रोज़मर्रा के लिए मोटे, सुर्ख़-स्लेटी सिक्के ढाल डाले।

panels.shot: tight close-up on a die being struck onto a warm lead blank
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer raises a small hammer and brings it down on a metal die pressed to a fresh lead blank, freezing the moment just as the impression begins to form.

dialogue.speaker: satavahana_moneyers
dialogue.text: Not just metal, but a promise from king to subject.

i18n.hi: यह सिर्फ़ धातु नहीं, राजा से प्रजा तक का वादा था।

panels.shot: macro shot of several finished lead coins, showing symbols like Ujjain-type cross, chaitya and early legends
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer arranges a handful of newly struck lead coins on a wooden tray, their surfaces bearing small symbols of rails, chaitya arches and early Brahmi legends around central devices.

dialogue.text: On these lead rounds they stamped old regional signs, new legends and royal marks, knitting local habits into imperial design.

i18n.hi: इन सीसे के चक्करों पर पुराने प्रादेशिक चिन्ह, नई लिखाइयाँ और शाही निशान काटे गए, स्थानीय रीतों को साम्राज्य की सजावट में पिरोते हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot of a Deccan town street, small traders passing chunky lead coins hand to hand
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer watches in satisfaction as a potter pays a weaver with thick lead coins, while a tax collector further down the street accepts similar pieces from a line of townsfolk.

dialogue.text: These lead coins moved through inland markets and tax offices, their weight and stamp more valuable than the crude metal alone.

i18n.hi: ये सीसे के सिक्के भीतरू बाज़ारों और कर-दफ़्तरों में घूमे, उनका वज़न और ठप्पा कच्ची धातु से ज़्यादा कीमती बना।

panels.shot: interior of a more refined mint, with smaller copper and potin blanks alongside lead pieces
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer stands between trays: one piled with large lead blanks, another with smaller, reddish copper discs, and a third with greyish potin pieces ready for striking.

dialogue.text: Beside lead, they struck copper and potin, mixing base metals to create lighter coins, finer for some payments and regions.

i18n.hi: सीसे के साथ ही ताँबे और पॉटिन के सिक्के भी बने, साधारण धातुएँ मिलाकर हल्के सिक्के, कुछ भुगतानों और इलाकों के लिए ज़्यादा नफ़ीस।

panels.shot: close-up of three coins side by side: a thick lead piece, a smaller potin, and a rarer silver coin
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer lays three coins in a line on a cloth: a thick lead piece, a medium-sized potin, and a small but bright silver coin, each distinct in size and shine.

dialogue.text: The system grew layered. Heavy lead for local trade, mixed-metal potin and copper for finer exchange, occasional silver for special, high-trust needs.

i18n.hi: सिस्टम परतदार हो गया—स्थानीय सौदे के लिए भारी सीसा, बारीक लेन-देन को पॉटिन और ताँबा, और कभी–कभार ख़ास भरोसे के लिए चाँदी।

panels.shot: map-like overhead shot with coins placed over western Deccan towns, showing different coin types clustered
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer leans over a map, placing lead coins over inland Deccan towns and smaller potin and copper pieces near river crossings and caravan hubs.

dialogue.text: Archaeologists now trace this pattern in the soil. Lead coins cluster in Deccan heartlands, other metals thicken along routes and towns tied into wider flows.

i18n.hi: पुरातत्वविद अब मिट्टी से यही पैटर्न पढ़ते हैं—दक्कन के दिल में सीसे के ढेर, और दूसरी धातुएँ उन राहों और कस्बों पर गाढ़ी, जो बड़े बहावों से जुड़ते थे।

panels.shot: dramatic coastal wide shot with ships anchored off a Satavahana port, warehouses and hills behind
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer stands on a raised platform at a busy western port, watching wooden ships at anchor as porters carry bales from wharfs to warehouses backed by Deccan hills.

dialogue.text: To the west, ports faced the Arabian Sea. Foreign merchants came for cotton, spices and stones, bringing Roman coins, glass and wine in return.

i18n.hi: पश्चिम में बंदरगाहों के सामने अरब सागर था; परदेसी व्यापारी कपास, मसाले और रत्नों के लिए आते, बदले में रोमन सिक्के, काँच और मदिरा लाते।

panels.shot: closer shot at the waterfront, an Indian merchant and a foreign trader examining Satavahana coins alongside Roman ones
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer watches as a local merchant spreads Satavahana coins on a crate beside gleaming Roman aurei and denarii, while a foreign trader gestures, comparing their sizes and designs.

dialogue.text: Satavahana coins mingled with Roman gold and silver, but each served different worlds: one for empire’s own circuits, the other for long-distance luxury trades.

i18n.hi: सातवाहन सिक्के रोमन सोने-चाँदी के साथ घुलमिल चले, पर उनकी दुनिया अलग थी—एक साम्राज्य की अपनी दौड़ के लिए, दूसरा दूर के ऐश-ओ-आराम के सौदों के लिए।

panels.shot: tight profile of the Moneyer examining a new die with a ship motif carved on it
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer holds up a freshly carved die showing a stylised ship with raised prow and simple cabins, inspecting its lines in the light of a nearby lamp.

dialogue.text: In this coastal world another symbol rose: the ship. Not proof of war fleets, but a sign of sea routes, ports and maritime pride.

i18n.hi: इसी तटीय दुनिया में एक और निशान उभरा—जहाज़; यह जंगी बेड़ों का सबूत नहीं, बल्कि समुंदर-राहों, बंदरगाहों और समुद्री गर्व की छाप था।

panels.shot: macro close-up of a ship-type coin of Vasishthiputra Pulumavi being struck, the ship design crisp
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer presses the ship die to a blank and strikes, revealing a crisp image of a multi-oared vessel on the coin surface, with traces of legend around it.

dialogue.text: Under rulers like Vasishthiputra Pulumavi, ship coins appeared, their find-spots echoing port zones named in inscriptions and texts.

i18n.hi: वसिष्ठिपुत्र पुलुमावि जैसे शासकों के ज़माने में जहाज़ वाले सिक्के दिखे, जिनकी मिले-जगहें शिलालेखों और ग्रंथों में वर्णित बंदरगाह इलाकों से मेल खाती हैं।

panels.shot: split-scene style wide shot: ship coins changing hands at a coastal market; lead coins in an inland town
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer stands between two scenes: on one side, a coastal trader hands over ship-type coins at a wharf; on the other, an inland farmer pays taxes with thick lead pieces in a dusty town.

dialogue.text: The imagery signalled orientation. Ship coins spoke to ports and coastal trade; lead coins continued to anchor inland markets and dues.

i18n.hi: यह तस्वीरें दिशा दिखाती थीं—जहाज़ वाले सिक्के बंदरगाहों और तटीय व्यापार से बात करते, सीसे के सिक्के भीतरू बाज़ारों और लगान को थामे रहते।

panels.shot: interior of a small monastery or shrine storeroom, monks handling donations of coins and goods
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer observes monks in a shrine storeroom counting piles of lead and copper coins alongside baskets of grain and cloth, stacking them carefully near inscription tablets.

dialogue.text: Even in religious gifts, coins did not erase barter. Shrines received metal alongside grain, cloth and labour, all woven into the same economy.

i18n.hi: धार्मिक दान में भी सिक्कों ने सीधा लेन-देन नहीं मिटाया; देवालयों को धातु के साथ अनाज, कपड़ा और मज़दूरी मिली, सब एक ही अर्थव्यवस्था में बुना हुआ।

panels.shot: time-lapse style shot with weathered coins half-buried in earth, a modern archaeologist’s hand brushing them aside, overlapped by the Moneyer’s ghostly figure
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer’s faint image hovers above modern hands brushing soil from corroded lead and ship-type coins, lying half-buried in an archaeological trench.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, corroded lead pieces and worn ship coins resurface, letting scholars map how the Satavahanas tied mines, markets and maritime worlds together.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद यही जंग लगे सीसे के टुकड़े और घिसे जहाज़ वाले सिक्के फिर निकलते हैं, ताकि विद्वान देख सकें कि सातवाहनों ने खदान, हाट और समुंदर की दुनिया को कैसे जोड़ा।

panels.shot: low, reflective mid-shot of the Moneyer in the quiet mint, empty furnaces behind, a single coin in his palm
panels.action: Satavahana Moneyer stands alone in a silent mint, furnaces dark, gazing at a single heavy lead coin resting in his open palm as light falls through a high lattice.

dialogue.text: By choosing local lead and stamping ships for the sea, the Satavahana moneyers showed how empires can mint innovation from the materials beneath their feet and the horizons they dare to imagine.

i18n.hi: स्थानीय सीसा चुनकर और समुद्र के लिए जहाज़ ठोककर सातवाहन मुद्रा-कारों ने दिखाया कि साम्राज्य अपने पैरों के नीचे की चीज़ों और आँखों के क्षितिज से कैसी नई गढ़न ढाल सकते हैं।

title_i18n.en: Lead, Potin and the Ship Coins
title_i18n.hi: सीसा, पॉटिन और जहाज़ वाले सिक्के

subtitle_i18n.en: How the Deccan Forged Wealth from Heavy Lead and Distant Seas
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे दक्कन ने भारी सीसे और दूर समुंदरों से दौलत गढ़ी
